title: Federal Duck Stamp Act of 2014
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on November 17, 2014. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Federal Duck Stamp Act of 2014 - (Sec. 2) Amends the Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp Act to increase the price of duck stamps, which are required to hunt migratory waterfowl, from $15 to $25.

Authorizes the Department of the Interior to reduce the price of stamps for a hunting year if the increase in the stamp price resulted in a reduction in revenues deposited in the Migratory Bird Conservation Fund.

Establishes a subaccount in the Fund to be used by Interior to acquire easements for the conservation of migratory birds. Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer all amounts in excess of $15 from the sale of each stamp to the subaccount.

(Sec. 3) Requires Interior to include in an annual report of the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission an assessment of the status of wetlands conservation projects for migratory bird conservation purposes, including an accounting of all expenditures made for acquisition of federal lands and an analysis of whether refuge lands are opened or closed for hunting and fishing.

(Sec. 4) Allows rural Alaska residents to take migratory waterfowl for subsistence uses without a duck stamp.

summary.headline: This law raises the federal duck stamp price from $15 to $25, directs the extra money to a bird habitat fund, and exempts rural Alaska subsistence hunters from the stamp requirement.
summary.what_it_does: Hunters who take migratory waterfowl must buy a federal duck stamp, and this law raises its price from $15 to $25. Money from each stamp above $15 goes to a new subaccount in the Migratory Bird Conservation Fund, which the Interior Department can use to buy easements that protect migratory bird habitat. The Interior Department may lower the price for a hunting year if the increase causes a drop in fund revenue. The law also requires an annual report on wetlands projects and refuge hunting and fishing access, and it lets rural Alaska residents hunt waterfowl for subsistence without a stamp.

who_it_affects.group: Duck hunters who buy federal waterfowl stamps
who_it_affects.how: They must pay $25 for a duck stamp instead of $15, unless the Interior Department lowers the price for a given hunting year.

who_it_affects.group: Rural Alaska residents who hunt waterfowl for subsistence
who_it_affects.how: They can take migratory waterfowl for subsistence uses without buying a duck stamp.

who_it_affects.group: Department of the Interior and the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission
who_it_affects.how: They must set up the new subaccount, use it to acquire conservation easements, and include wetlands and refuge access details in an annual report.

who_it_affects.group: Hunters and anglers who use national wildlife refuges
who_it_affects.how: The annual report must state whether refuge lands are opened or closed for hunting and fishing, which makes that information public.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 18, 2014. The summary does not give a separate start date for the higher stamp price or the other provisions.
